skills.name: What to change and what to measure
Fair tests
skills.description: Changing one thing and keeping the rest the same.

SCI_CHANGE_VS_MEASURE.label: Mixes up what you change and what you measure
SCI_CHANGE_VS_MEASURE.explanation: Chooses the result (e.g. plant height) as the thing to change.

SCI_CHANGE_MANY.label: Thinks changing more than one thing at once is fine
SCI_CHANGE_MANY.explanation: Doesn't see that two changes make the result impossible to explain.

SCI_KEEP_TESTED_SAME.label: Keeps the thing being tested the same
SCI_KEEP_TESTED_SAME.explanation: Lists the variable under test as something to control.

questions.prompt: Kabir is testing whether the type of surface affects how far a ball rolls. Which of these must stay the same to make it a fair test?
hints: In a fair test you change ONE thing and keep everything else the same.
Never keep the thing you are testing the same: you have to change it to test it.

options: The distance the ball rolls
The ball used
The type of surface

If the result changes, we can't tell which one caused it, so it isn't fair.

variables_in_investigations.title: What to change and what to measure
variables_in_investigations.big_idea: Every investigation asks 'Does A affect B?'. A is the one thing you change on purpose. B is the result you measure. Mixing them up means you can't answer the question.
steps: The first blank is what you change.
The second blank is what you measure.
Everything else is kept the same.
variables_in_investigations.sense_check: To find out if water affects plant growth, you give plants different amounts of water and measure their height, not the other way round.

worked_examples.prompt: Does the amount of water affect how tall a bean plant grows? What do you change?
steps: The question names the amount of water as the possible cause.
So that is what you change.

fair_test.title: Fair tests
fair_test.big_idea: A test is fair when only ONE thing changes, the thing being tested. Everything else that could affect the result is kept the same, so any difference must be caused by that one thing.
steps: Name the thing you are testing: it must change.
List other things that could affect the result.
Keep all of those the same.
If two things change at once, you can't tell which caused the result.
fair_test.sense_check: If you change both the ramp height and the car, and the car goes further, was it the ramp or the car? You can't tell.

worked_examples.prompt: Testing whether ramp height affects how far a car rolls. Keep the same?
worked_examples.answer: The car and the floor surface
steps: Ramp height is tested, so it changes.
The car and the floor could also change the distance.
